rci1_using_msad.detail: Multi-site; EU-AIMS LEAP dataset collected across 6 collaborating sites in 4 countries (KCL London, Cambridge, Nijmegen, Utrecht, Mannheim, Rome) with 6 different 3T MRI scanners from 3 manufacturers (GE, Siemens, Philips)
rci1_using_msad.supporting_text: "Participants underwent comprehensive clinical, cognitive and MRI assessment at one of six collaborating sites."

rci2_using_epd.detail: EU-AIMS LEAP (Longitudinal European Autism Project) dataset used for normative model training
rci2_using_epd.supporting_text: "we leveraged the unique, large-scale and deeply phenotyped EU-AIMS Longitudinal European Autism Project 47,48 (LEAP), which is the largest European multicenter initiative aimed at identifying biomarkers in autism."

rci3_epd_name.detail: EU-AIMS/AIMS-2-TRIALS LEAP cohort; full sample with complete imaging data across four modalities (structural MRI, rs-fMRI, task-fMRI, EEG) and phenotypic information
rci3_epd_name.supporting_text: "All participants were part of the EU-AIMS/AIMS-2-TRIALS Longitudinal European Autism Project (LEAP) cohort."

model-1.model-name: multimodal normative models (structure, rs-fMRI, task-fMRI, EEG) for FFG

rci5_n.detail: Overall phase (10-fold cross-validation across entire sample); normative models were trained across all individuals (99 autistic + 105 NAI), not exclusively on healthy controls. Separate normative models were estimated per modality per hemisphere (8 models total) but all shared the same sample.
rci5_n.supporting_text: "normative models were trained across all individuals using Bayesian Linear Regression (BLR)" ; "Normative models were derived in an unbiased manner under 10-fold cross-validation."
